candidate.answerReason: The equal-time equation gives x=6. The production rates are then 6 and 8 items per day, and both durations are 10 days.

methods.label: Equate production times
methods.explanation: Set up the equation \(\frac{60}{x}=\frac{80}{x+2}\). Clearing the denominators gives \(60(x+2)=80x\), so \(x=6\). Checking confirms that it satisfies the conditions of the problem.
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 8 rational-equation solving followed by a Grade 7 linear equation.

methods.label: Find the common duration
methods.explanation: Over the same duration, B makes \(80-60=20\) more items because B makes 2 more items each day. Thus the common duration is \(20\div2=10\) days. A therefore makes \(x=60\div10=6\) items per day. B makes 8 items per day, consistent with making 80 items in those 10 days.
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary differences and division to recover the common duration and then the daily output.
